paper.title: Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER with OC22
paper.file_name: 38_Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER with OC22.pdf
paper.research_summary: This work uses pre-trained machine learning models from the Open Catalyst 2022 (OC22) framework to interpolate total energy predictions for OER surface intermediates on 4119 oxide materials, enabling high-throughput screening for viable anode catalysts under bulk and nanoscale Pourbaix stability, overpotential, material cost, and metastability constraints.

tasks.task_name_raw: Rational design of nanoscale stabilized oxide catalysts for OER
tasks.objective: Identify viable candidate anode catalysts for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) under varying reaction conditions including bulk, surface, and nanoscale Pourbaix stability, material cost, overpotential, and metastability.
constraints: material cost less than RuO2 ($18315 per kg)
energy above hull ≤ 0.1 eV per atom
input_requirements: DFT-calculated surface energies and OER binding energies
output_goal: 190 candidate materials (122 bulk and 68 nanostable) for OER
freely available database of ML-predicted structures and energies

evidence.text: In this work, we interpolated a database of the total energy predictions for all slabs and OER surface intermediates for 4119 oxide materials in the original OC22 dataset using pre-trained models from the OC22 framework. This database includes all terminations of all facets up to a maximum Miller index of 1. To demonstrate the full utility of this database, we constructed a flexible screening framework to identify viable candidate anode catalysts for OER under varying reaction conditions for bulk, surface, and nanoscale Pourbaix stability as well as material cost, overpotential, and metastability.

stages.stage_name_raw: Obtaining bulk materials from Materials Project
stages.stage_goal: Acquire bulk crystal structures for slab construction.
stage_output: bulk materials used for slab construction

evidence.text: The bulk materials used for slab construction in this study were obtained from the Materials Project.

stages.stage_goal: Construct slabs for all facets up to maximum Miller index of 1, including all terminations while maintaining equivalent surfaces on both sides.
stage_output: slabs with atomic and vacuum layers ~12.5 Å thick
non-stoichiometric slabs with respect to bulk formula

evidence.text: We described all facets up to a MMI of 1 containning an atomic and vacuum layer of ca. 12.5 Å thick. The bulk materials used for slab construction in this study were obtained from the Materials Project. We also considered all terminations for each facet (sans slabs exceeding 200 atoms) while maintaining equivalent surfaces on both sides of the slab which consequently resulted in non-stoichiometric slabs with respect to the bulk formula.

stages.stage_goal: Fine-tune pre-trained S2EF-Total model on OC22 dataset to better predict total energies of oxide surfaces and surface intermediates.

evidence.text: We used a pre-trained model for the Structure to Energy and Forces (S2EF)-Total task from the OC22 framework to perform all machine learning predictions of the relaxed structure and total energy. The entirety of the Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) dataset (1281040 DFT relaxations) was used to train an S2EF-Total model which was subsequently fine-tuned with the OC22 dataset (62331 DFT relaxations) to better predict the total energies of oxide surfaces and surface intermediates.

stages.stage_name_raw: Interpolating total energy predictions for slabs and surface intermediates
stages.stage_goal: Systematically extrapolate total DFT energy of all terminations for all facets up to MMI = 1 for all 4119 materials, and extrapolate total energy of all metal adsorption sites on all surfaces for O*, OH*, and OOH*.
stage_output: interpolated database of total energies for 4119 materials

evidence.text: Using the previously developed ML models, we systematically extrapolated the total DFT energy of all terminations for all facets up to a MMI = 1 for all 4119 materials considered in this study.
Table 1 summarizes the scope of our extrapolated database.

stages.stage_goal: Screen candidates using tiered criteria: (1) presence in OC22 training set, (2) Pourbaix stability, (3) Wulff shape surface stability, (4) overpotential < 0.75 V, (5) energy above hull ≤ 0.1 eV/atom, (6) material cost < $8346/kg.

evidence.text: From our assessment, we were able to identify 122 and 68 viable candidates for OER under the bulk and nanoscale regime, respectively.

stages.stage_goal: Validate ML-predicted Gibbs adsorption energies and overpotentials against DFT calculations for selected compounds.
stage_input: DFT-calculated ΔGads values for 33 Pourbaix stable compounds

evidence.text: We used DFT to validate 85 values for Gibbs adsorption energy corresponding to eqn (6)–(8) for 33 Pourbaix stable compounds in our database. The MAE of the test set shown in Fig. 7(a) is 0.42 which is larger than the MAE of 0.239 eV obtained from the validation set in the original OC22 assessment.
The bulk materials used for slab construction in this study were obtained from the Materials Project.

The entirety of the Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) dataset (1281040 DFT relaxations) was used to train an S2EF-Total model which was subsequently fine-tuned with the OC22 dataset (62331 DFT relaxations) to better predict the total energies of oxide surfaces and surface intermediates.

More recently, the Open Catalyst 2022 (OC22) framework has expanded upon this dataset by incorporating random combinations of 4732 oxide materials, Miller indices up to 3, and surface intermediates involved in OER.
